keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Tasmania including its Bass Strait islands (233 land cells, about 59,000 km2): after the flooding of Bass Strait the island and its Aboriginal people were isolated "for about 8,000 years"; the page gives no area for the pre-contact territory, only nine nations of 6-15 clans (3,000 to 15,000 people).

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): Tasmania is cut off and its Aboriginal people are isolated. "Around 6000 BCE, rising sea levels flooded the Bass Strait and separated Tasmania from mainland Australia"; they "remained isolated from mainland Aboriginal populations for approximately 8,000 years". The page elsewhere says the Bassian Plain was submerged "between about 14,000 and 12,000 BCE" and that people crossed into Tasmania "approximately 35,000 years ago".

ledger.note: 3400 BCE (end of the cultures horizon): the dossier stops here but the Aboriginal Tasmanians continue. The dossier stops at -3400, the horizon of the cultures group (Cliopatria holds nothing before 3400 BCE and no later group draws this land until the colonies); the culture itself does not end there. The page has them isolated and unchanged "Before British colonisation in 1803".

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border; the nations inside are not mapped on the page.

sources.title: Aboriginal Tasmanians
sources.note: Bass Strait flooded around 6000 BCE; isolation about 8,000 years; nine nations, 3,000-15,000 people; British colonisation in 1803.

notes: Aboriginal Tasmanians. The page contradicts itself on when Tasmania was cut off (6000 BCE against 14,000-12,000 BCE for the submerging of the Bassian Plain): the 6000 BCE sentence is used for the start. The dossier ends at -3400 by the group's convention although the page carries the isolation to British colonisation in 1803 ("Before British colonisation in 1803, Tasmanian Aboriginal communities maintained distinct languages"; first settlement at Risdon Cove on South East Aboriginal land); extending the end to 1803 with the successor colony-of-tasmania (suggested by oc-02-a) is a one-line change. King Island and the Furneaux Group groups "later died out" (undated on the page).
